why: A one-screen layout is the clearest 'this is a real DAW' signal and fixes today's biggest laptop pain (tracks 1,700 px down). Every serious DAW (Live, Bitwig, FL) is a fixed window with a centre canvas and toggleable side and bottom panels, and AI-first studios (Suno Studio 2.0 Chat, FL Gopher) keep the assistant one panel away from the timeline. The risk is size: step 1 is L, moves many nodes, and depends on UX-4 landing first.
improve: Make every panel toggle with one shortcut and remember it, like Live's Browser/Detail toggles; that matters more than default sizes
On 1366x768 start with the controller drawer hidden and the docked editor closed, so tracks get at least 300 px
Keep the Keys sidebar foldable to the orb rail and test that voice still works while folded
